translationRepairs: An edict said: "In highest antiquity the supreme ruler soothed the age through virtue; the Change was plain and without elaborate culture.
An edict said: "In highest antiquity the supreme ruler soothed the age through virtue; rule was easy and plain, without elaborate culture.
易簡 is the classical pair “easy and simple” for unadorned rule, not the Book of Changes; the old literal invents “the Change.”
I have heard that in high antiquity worthies yielded their thrones and instruction was of one virtue; hence the Change was plain and the people were transformed.
I have heard that in high antiquity worthies yielded their thrones and instruction was of one virtue; hence rule was easy and plain and the people were transformed.
The same 易簡 again means easy, plain government, not the Changes; Xi Shen’s answer matches the edict’s wording.

While his mother lived she had no cart for travel; after her death he refused to haul her coffin by wagon—too poor to buy horses he laid her in temporary burial outside the north wall of his hall, cut a doorway through, and mourned morning and night.

When Shen's mother fell ill, they suffered from having no cart; after she died he did not want the coffin carried by wagon—too poor to buy horses, he laid her in a temporary burial outside the north wall of the hall where he dwelt, opened a door, and bowed and wept morning and night.
詵母病 names illness before 苦無車; the old idiomatic line treats the lack of a cart as a lifetime condition and drops the illness.
He rose to Gentleman of the Secretariat, then became adjutant to the household attendant for chariots and cavalry.
He was transferred to Gentleman of the Secretariat, then became adjutant to the General of Chariots and Cavalry.
徙 is a transfer, and 車騎從事中郎 is the staff gentleman of the chariot-and-cavalry command, not a household attendant.
Hence the Odes praises 'the Xianyun blaze fiercely'; the Documents sighs 'barbarians lead in submission.
Hence the Odes praises 'the Xianyun blaze fiercely'; the Documents sighs 'barbarians lead in submission.'
The Chinese closes the Documents quotation and the sentence; the old English leaves the second quote unclosed.

Under Xuandi and Yuandi, Zhao Chongguo subdued the western Qiang and Feng Fengshi the southern Qiang—both without drawing blood, crushing bullies and seizing ringleaders: real containment of disaster with costs and gains plain—the middle Han at its clearest."

Under Xuandi and Yuandi, Zhao Chongguo subdued the Xiling Qiang and Feng Fengshi the southern Qiang—both without drawing blood, crushing bullies and seizing ringleaders: real containment of disaster with costs and gains plain—the middle Han at its clearest."
西零 is the Xiling ethnonym parallel to 南羌, not a generic “western Qiang.”

河內 is Henei, 南陽太守 is Prefect of Nanyang, and 二千石 is the two-thousand-bushel rank, not “Hanoi” or a generic “governor.”

Great Jin rose on time—Emperor Wen mapped strategy—peace fell into line;
Great Jin rose on time—the Literary Emperor laid plans—Anle submitted and followed the track;
安樂順軌 names Anle’s submission, not abstract peace; 文皇 is the Literary Emperor who laid the plans.
When great Jin dragon rose, answering the period and receiving the mandate—Literary Emperor laid plans—peace and joy followed the track;
When great Jin dragon rose, answering the period and receiving the mandate—Literary Emperor laid plans—Anle followed the track;
安樂 is the Anle title, not “peace and joy.”
Liu Song, chief justice of his county, sighed, "Who knew our town held such a mind!"
Liu Song of the same commandery, then Commandant of Justice, sighed on seeing him: "I did not realize my village held such talent!"
同郡 marks shared commandery origin and 廷尉 is the central Commandant of Justice, not a county chief justice.

Gan Zhuo once was seized by Sima Yue, Prince of Donghai—who issued an order that whoever harbored him would be executed—Zhuo threw himself on Tan and escaped.
司馬越 is Sima Yue, Prince of Donghai; 下令 is his order that harborers be executed.

At the beginning of Jianxing, Emperor Yuan appointed him army libationer-consultant.
建興初 dates the appointment; 元帝 is Emperor Yuan, not a person named Jianxing Yuan.

At the beginning of Jianxing, Emperor Yuan appointed him Libationer Consultant of the Army Defending the East.
元帝 is Emperor Yuan; 鎮東 modifies the army office 軍諮祭酒, not a princely title “of the east.”
Hua Changfeng served as conquer-barbarians marshal against Ji Sang and died fighting.
Hua, courtesy name Changfeng, served as Marshal Who Conquers Barbarians, campaigned against Ji Sang, and died in battle.
化字長風 separates given name 化 from courtesy name 長風; the old line fuses them into one English name.
Hua Tan lived by duty like Zhou Fu and Gan Zhuo—kind men reach far—so goes the verdict.
Ling Si conducted himself by righteousness; his will was earnest toward Zhou and Gan—perhaps this is what is meant by the benevolent man penetrating!
The appraisal’s subject is courtesy name 令思, and 周、甘 is written as that pair; the old line substitutes Hua Tan and expands the surnames while compressing 仁者必通.
